chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abū al-Ḥasan, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one of our companions, from al-Riḍā (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a Christian who became a Muslim, and with him was wine and pigs, and upon him was a debt. Can he sell his wine and his pigs and pay off his debt? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a convert's wine and pigs regarding debt payment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) rules that a newly converted Christian who possesses wine and pigs cannot sell them to pay off his debts, implying that the items remain in his possession as a form of holding rather than being liquidated. This ruling highlights the distinction between the impurity of the item and the obligation of debt repayment, suggesting that the convert retains the assets until a more appropriate method of disposal or payment is determined, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the time. The decision underscores the principle that conversion does not immediately alter the legal status of existing assets, but rather their permissibility and handling.
